sections.heading: What Oil Tank Removal Costs in Moncton
sections.html:
For a standard aboveground tank beside the house or in a garage, expect $500 to $1,500. That range covers the whole job, not just hauling the steel away. Here's what's included:

  • Pumping out and properly disposing of any residual oil
  • Disconnecting and capping the fill, vent, and supply lines
  • Removing the tank and hauling it for recycling
  • A written record of the removal for your files or insurer

Where you land in that range depends on access, tank size, and how much oil is left inside. A basement tank costs extra because it usually has to be drained and cut apart to get up the stairs, and we'll quote that clearly up front. If your tank is underground, that's a different job with excavation involved, and our buried oil tank removal page walks through what to expect.

If you're weighing removal against a swap to a new tank, our tank replacement cost guide lays out both sets of numbers so you can compare.

sections.heading: Removing Your Tank for a Heat Pump? The OHPA Grant Helps
sections.html:
A lot of the removals we do in Moncton, Dieppe, and Riverview these days are for homeowners leaving oil heat behind entirely. If that's you, there's good news. The federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (OHPA) program offers up to $10,000 toward switching from oil to a cold-climate heat pump, and it explicitly lists safe removal of your oil tank as an eligible cost.

That means the tank removal you'd need to do anyway can be rolled into your grant claim instead of coming out of pocket. We provide a clear written invoice that spells out the removal work, which is exactly what the program paperwork asks for.

One practical tip: don't have the tank pulled before you've confirmed your program details and timing. Do it in the order your grant requires, keep every receipt, and the process goes smoothly. We're happy to schedule around your heat pump installer.

sections.heading: What Happens to Your Old Tank
sections.html:
People ask this a lot, and it's a fair question. First, we pump out whatever oil is still in the tank. Even a tank that reads empty usually holds a few centimetres of oil and sludge at the bottom, and that residue goes to a licensed facility for proper disposal, never down a drain or into the ground.

Then we disconnect and cap the lines so there's no way for a delivery driver to accidentally fill a tank that isn't there anymore. It sounds unlikely, but misdirected fills happen every year in New Brunswick, and a capped fill pipe is cheap insurance against a very expensive cleanup.

The tank itself gets loaded up and taken to a metal recycler, where the steel is processed and reused. Nothing sits in a ditch or a back lot. If you want photos of the empty spot and the tank on the truck for your insurance file, just ask and we'll send them along.

sections.heading: How a Removal Day Goes
sections.html:
Most aboveground removals are done in a single morning. Here's the usual rhythm:

  • Free written estimate. We look at the tank, the access, and the oil level, then give you a firm price.
  • Pump out. Residual oil and sludge come out first, into sealed containers.
  • Disconnect. Fill, vent, and supply lines are cut back and capped.
  • Remove and haul. The tank goes on the truck, whole or in sections if it's a basement unit.
  • Clean up and paperwork. We sweep up, and you get documentation of the removal.

We handle removals across the region, from Moncton out to Shediac, Salisbury, Memramcook, and Sackville. And if you're calling because the tank is actively leaking, skip the queue and use our 24/7 emergency line instead. Leaks can't wait for a scheduled appointment.

faq.q: How much does oil tank removal cost in Moncton?
faq.a: Most aboveground removals run $500 to $1,500, and that includes disconnecting the lines and disposing of any leftover oil. Basement tanks cost a bit more because they have to be drained and cut apart to get out. Buried tanks are a separate job with excavation, so they're priced differently. Every job starts with a free written estimate, so you'll have your exact number before we begin.

faq.q: How long does it take to remove an oil tank?
faq.a: A typical aboveground tank comes out in 2 to 3 hours, start to finish. Basement tanks usually take 3 to 5 hours because of the draining, cutting, and carrying involved. Either way, most removals are wrapped up the same day we arrive.

faq.q: What do you do with the oil left in my tank?
faq.a: We pump it out before the tank moves an inch. Even a tank that looks empty often holds 20 to 40 litres of oil and sludge at the bottom. All of it goes to a licensed facility for proper disposal, and that's included in your $500 to $1,500 price, not billed as an extra.

faq.q: Does the federal heat pump grant cover tank removal?
faq.a: Yes. The Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (OHPA) program offers up to $10,000 for switching from oil to a heat pump, and safe removal of your oil tank is explicitly listed as an eligible expense. Keep our written invoice with your grant paperwork and the removal can be covered as part of your claim. Just confirm your program timing before booking so everything happens in the right order.

faq.q: My old tank is buried in the yard. Is that the same service?
faq.a: No, buried tanks are a different job. They involve excavation, checking the soil around the tank, and filling in the hole afterward, so they cost more than the $500 to $1,500 aboveground range. We handle those too, and the process is covered on our buried oil tank removal page. The free written estimate works the same way for both.
